correctness.rationale: This PASS is for the complete corrected files in /workspace/repairs/3/. In the frozen proof, line 68 bounded the sum over integers m>Y by the tail integral from Y, which is not valid for arbitrary nonintegral Y. For example, when a=3 and Y=29/10, the terms m=3,4,5 alone sum to more than 1/(2Y²) before multiplying by X. The corrected proof starts at L=floor(Y)+1, retaining the first term and bounding the rest by the integral from L. This gives at most Y^a+Y^(a+1)/(a−1), uniformly O(X^(2/3)) for a>=3; for Y<2 the sum starts at 2 and the corrected integral estimate is at most X·2^(−a)(1+2/(a−1))<2√X. I reconstructed the other steps: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2606.22997v1 has k=n−1>=2 and gives D=1 iff n/M>M; negation gives the stated criterion. Distinct exact blocks are coprime and have product dividing n, so two cannot be at least √n. An exponent-one dominant block would violate P^+(n)<=√n, since equality would force n=p². For a>=2 and n=p^a b with b<=p^a and p not dividing b, p²<=n and every other prime q has q²<=b²<=n, proving the converse. The floor formula counts b<=min(p^a,X/p^a) excluding multiples of p exactly. At Y=X^(1/(2a)), partial summation with the prime number theorem gives Y^(a+1)/((a+1)log Y) and X·Y^(1−a)/((a−1)log Y) for the leading pieces. The floor and far-tail errors are O_a(X^(1/a)); the two coprimality corrections are O_a(X^(1/2)). Both exponents are strictly below (a+1)/(2a) for any fixed a>=2. Conversion from log Y gives 4a²/(a²−1). The corrected uniform estimate sums over at most log_2 X exponents, giving o(X^(3/4)/log X) beyond the a=2 layer, whose coefficient is 16/3. The verification notes now distinguish the direct binomial-GCD check from the five cutoff comparisons; no uploaded code was run or needed to prove the asymptotic.
residual_risks: The layer equivalents hold for fixed a only; the uniform tail bound is not a uniform equivalent. Finite checks cover only their reported ranges and cutoffs.

value.rationale: The square-root cutoff is intrinsic to the imported exact GCD criterion. Removing the large-prime cases isolates the place where nontriviality depends on higher exact prime powers; quantifying that exception with a power-law scale, a sharp constant, and disjoint layer equivalents is substantially more informative than zero density or finite counts alone. The corrected proof keeps these findings and the boundary unchanged.
residual_risks: No exact positive GCD-value frequencies or asymptotic for exponents growing with X are claimed.
